top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The presence of tortuous and coiled vascular channels with early filling of the renal vein on arteriography, along with the patient's symptoms of right flank pain and significant hematuria, support this diagnosis. The initial concern for a blood clot was resolved with further investigation.

Although the CT scan revealed a small soft tissue mass within the right renal pelvis and the patient presented with hematuria, the lack of significant enhancement after contrast medium injection and the subsequent findings from the arteriography and other tests make this diagnosis less likely than Congenital Renal Arteriovenous Malformation.
